mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen monotonically from -41.1% to -30.6% over four weeks, signaling gradual return to office routines. This sustained upward trend in workplace commuting will drive increased retail-and-recreation visits during lunch hours and after-work shopping over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 10.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses direction and falls below -32% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 19.6% to 16.4% over four weeks, indicating people are spending less time at home and more time outside. This behavioral shift toward outdoor activity will translate into higher retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks as people resume discretionary shopping and entertainment.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 3.2 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases above 17.5% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has stabilized around -71% to -75% with minimal week-on-week volatility. When TRANSIT falls below -72% and remains flat for two consecutive weeks, it signals suppressed public transportation use that constrains retail access for transit-dependent populations, depressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -72% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -71.4% in t-0w, range -71.4% to -75.0%
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -70% within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined from -20.3% to -17.0% over four weeks while RETAIL_REC has improved from -37.3% to -35.6%. The joint recovery in outdoor recreation and retail suggests a coordinated behavioral shift toward discretionary mobility. Continued co-movement of PARKS and RETAIL_REC will sustain retail gains over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improving over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below -18% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously falls below -36%, indicating decoupling of the co-movement pattern.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained near baseline (-0.3% to -1.9%), indicating essential shopping is unaffected by restrictions. When essential shopping is stable and WORKPLACES begins recovering, policy restrictions are loosening. Under loosening policy regimes, RETAIL_REC will rise over the next four weeks as non-essential retail reopens.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within ±2% of baseline while WORKPLACES rises above -35%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable near zero, WORKPLACES at -30.6%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -5% or WORKPLACES falls below -35% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved 1.7 percentage points over four weeks from -37.3% to -35.6%, establishing a weak but consistent upward trend. This seasonal or cyclical recovery pattern will continue at the same rate, producing further gains of 1-2 percentage points over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -37.3% to -35.6% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls below -36% in any of the next two weeks, or the rate of improvement reverses to negative.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has declined from -75.0% to -71.4% over four weeks, showing a 3.6 percentage point recovery. If TRANSIT continues recovering and crosses above -70% within one week, it signals sufficient public transportation capacity restoration to enable retail access, triggering a one-week surge in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -70% in the next week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT does not rise above -70% within the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 1 percentage point in the week following TRANSIT crossing -70%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL mobility show inverse relationship: as WORKPLACES rises from -41.1% to -30.6%, RESIDENTIAL falls from 19.6% to 16.4%. This reallocation of time from home to work signals confidence in mobility resumption. When this pattern persists, RETAIL_REC will rise over the next two weeks as people combine work commutes with retail stops.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL cease moving in opposite directions, or RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days despite continued inverse movement.
